title: The Date That Turned Kaneki Into a Ghoul

cuts.voiceover_text: Every love story has a place where it starts. For Kaneki, a shy black-haired bookworm, it is this little coffee shop. His best friend Hide leans in, grinning, demanding to know which girl has him acting like this. Kaneki blushes hard and denies everything. It does not work. Hide turns to the waitress and asks her point blank if she is seeing anyone, and Kaneki nearly dies on the spot. He is mortified. Because this quiet shop is the only place he ever runs into her. The beautiful girl with purple hair who reads the exact same novels he does.

Days later, Kaneki walks the purple-haired girl home through the empty night streets. Her name is Rize. He stops, gathers every drop of courage he has, and forces the words out. He wants to see her again. Same taste in books, same age, it has to mean something. Rize turns, and she is smiling. The truth is, she says, she has had her eye on him too. Kaneki's whole face lights up in disbelief. He cannot believe his luck. Then the camera pushes in on her eyes behind those red glasses. Something in them glints. He does not see it. We do.

It was never a love story. Blood runs down Rize's chin as she slowly pulls off her glasses. Her eyes turn black and red. Kaneki stares up at her, frozen. He is terrified. Crimson tendrils explode from her back, and the girl he fell for starts hunting him through the dark construction site. He runs. It does not matter. She moves like something out of his horror novels, toying with him, pinning him, tearing into his side. Kaneki screams, blood streaming down his face as she slams him into the fence. The sweet bookworm was a ghoul the whole time. And he was always dinner.

Kaneki wakes up drowning in a red-lit dream, Rize's pale face drifting beside him in the water. Then the hospital. Machines. White walls. Through the fog he hears the doctors talking about him. A date with Rize. An emergency operation. A transplant, her organs, from the body next to him, into him. Kaneki's eyes go wide. What the hell are they talking about?

Then the evening news answers everything. An expert explains it calmly to the cameras. Ghouls cannot live on human food. Their tongues work differently than ours, so everything normal tastes disgusting to them. The only nutrition their bodies can accept is human flesh. Kaneki sits frozen in front of the screen. His food has tasted like garbage for days. He is sweating. He is doing the math in his head. And the answer terrifies him.

Days of starving later, it hits him on the street. A smell. Sweet, warm, familiar, almost like his mom's home cooking. For the first time since the hospital, something actually smells like food. Hope floods his face. He runs, following it through the dark alleys, nearly crying with relief. He finally found something he can eat. Then he rounds the corner. The sweet smell is coming from a corpse, a dead man lying in a pool of blood. Kaneki stops dead. His left eye has already turned black and red. His body knew what that smell was before he did. He is horrified.

The blue-haired waitress from the coffee shop crouches over him. The blue-haired waitress from the coffee shop crouches over him. Touka, a ghoul herself, fresh blood on her cheek from the fight she just finished. She recognizes him instantly. The guy who was with Rize. So why did Rize not eat him, she demands. And what is with that eye of his? Kaneki is shaking. He can barely look at her. You might find this hard to believe, he says, but I am actually human. And yet I want to eat that. Every part of me is screaming to shove it into my mouth. But I know I cannot. Because if I do, I stop being human. Touka stares at him, and for a second even she looks stunned.

Touka watches him crumble and loses patience. If it hurts that much, just eat. Kaneki sobs harder. No way. No way. He could never eat another person's flesh. He would have to kill to eat, and he will not, because he is human. He says it like a prayer he no longer believes. Touka's eyes go cold. You do not have the nerve to eat it on your own, she says. Then let me give you a hand. She bends down, takes the flesh, and moves toward him. Kaneki's red eye fills with tears. His old life is over.
